cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel before they go into the land God is giving them. Law after law, he's laying out how they're going to live there, and friend, this man has NOT run out of laws. Now he gets to marriage: if a man finds some indecency in his wife, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her and send her away.
Now say she leaves and becomes another man's wife. Then that second husband divorces her too, or he dies.

cards.question: True or false: once her second marriage ends, her first husband may marry her again.

cards.text: Next up, newlyweds. For one year, a newly married man must not be sent to war or pressed into any duty.

cards.question: A newlywed gets a whole year with no war and no duty. What is he free to do with it?

answers.text: Stay home and bring joy to his wife
Serve the priests at the tabernacle
Build a new house for his family

cards.text: The closest I ever got to a year off was the junk drawer, and NOBODY was bringing anybody joy in there. Next, loans: a lender must not take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper one, as security for a debt.

cards.question: Why can't a lender take a man's millstones as security for a debt?

answers.text: It would take his livelihood as security
Millstones belong to the whole town
They are too heavy to carry off

cards.question: Then Moses gets serious. If a man kidnaps a fellow Israelite and treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must ___.

cards.text: Then Moses turns to infectious skin diseases. He says be careful to follow every instruction from the ones he has given commands to about it.

cards.question: In cases of infectious skin disease, whose instructions does Moses tell Israel to follow?

answers.text: The elders at the city gate

cards.text: And Moses adds a reminder: remember what the LORD did to Miriam on the journey out of Egypt. Miriam, Moses' sister, was struck with a skin disease on that road (Numbers 12:10; 26:59).
Back to loans. When you lend your neighbor anything, you do not march into his house to collect the security.

cards.question: So where does the lender wait while his neighbor gets the security?

answers.text: Outside while he brings it out

cards.text: And if the borrower is a poor man, the lender must not go to sleep with his security still in hand.

cards.question: The lender is to return the poor man's security by ___, so he may sleep in his own cloak and bless him.
True or false: Moses says giving the poor man's security back will be credited as righteousness before the LORD.

cards.text: Moses keeps going, and now it's payday. Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he's an Israelite or a foreigner living in your towns.

cards.question: Moses says to pay a poor hired hand his wages each day before ___.
Why does Moses say a poor hired hand's pay can't wait?

answers.text: He is poor and depends on it
He might leave for another town

cards.text: Hold it back, and he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you'll be guilty of sin. So not "the check's in the mail," not "next Friday," friend, it's TODAY, TODAY, TODAY!

cards.question: True or false: under this law, children can be put to death for their fathers' sins.

cards.text: Moses says do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless. And do not take a widow's cloak as security.

cards.question: What reason does Moses give Israel for treating the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow this way?

answers.text: They were once slaves in Egypt
Foreigners bring trade to their towns
Widows can take them to the elders

cards.text: Harvest time, and you forget a sheaf out in the field. Friend, I once hunted an hour for my spatula, and it was in my MUSTACHE, I was HOLDING it.

cards.question: What does Moses say the farmer should do about that forgotten sheaf?

answers.text: Leave it behind for those in need
Go back for it before nightfall
Bring it to the priests as an offering

cards.question: Leave the forgotten sheaf, so the LORD your God may ___ you in all the work of your hands.
True or false: the same goes for olives and grapes, with no going over the branches or the vines a second time.

cards.text: And Moses brings back that reminder: remember you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That's why he's commanding all this.
Next, the courtroom. Disputes go before a judge, and if the guilty man deserves a beating, he gets the number of lashes his crime warrants, but no more than forty.

cards.question: Why does Moses cap a guilty man's beating at forty lashes?

answers.text: So his brother isn't degraded in their sight
So the judge can hear more cases
So the punishment ends by sunset

cards.question: Then Moses talks about an ox walking over the grain all day, treading it out. What does he say not to do to it?

answers.text: Let it eat the grain it treads
Work it after the sun goes down

cards.text: Working all day right next to a snack and can't have a bite? That's me beside a fresh tray of cookies, not allowed to sneak ONE. Now a family law: when brothers live together and one dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow.

cards.question: The first son the widow bears will carry on the name of the ___ brother.

cards.text: But what if the brother doesn't want to marry his brother's widow? Moses has that covered too.

cards.question: True or false: if the brother refuses, the widow takes it to the elders at the city gate.
The elders summon the brother, and he still says he doesn't want to marry her. In front of the elders, the widow takes something off him. What is it?

cards.text: A sandal! Friend, I don't even have feet, I have a gold base, and NOBODY is taking my base. Then she spits in his face and declares, “This is what is done to the man who will not maintain his brother’s line.”

cards.question: From then on, his family name in Israel will be called “The House of the ___.”

cards.text: Then a law about a fight. If a wife tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the attacker's genitals, her hand is to be cut off, with no pity shown.

Then business: no two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light, and no two differing measures in your house. That's a baker with a BIG scoop for buying chocolate chips and a teeny tiny scoop for selling them.

cards.question: Moses says Israel must keep accurate and honest weights and measures. Why?

answers.text: So they may live long in the land
So the priests get a fair tithe
So the king can tax them fairly

cards.question: True or false: Moses says everyone who is dishonest with weights and measures is detestable to the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses gives one more thing to remember: the Amalekites, who attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17:8). They met Israel on the journey from Egypt, when everyone was tired and weary.

cards.question: Israel is tired and weary on the road. Who do the Amalekites attack?
True or false: Moses says once the LORD gives Israel rest from their enemies, they can forget what Amalek did.

cards.text: Instead, Moses says to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. And friend, Moses is NOT done preaching yet, so keep that oven warm.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 10 quotes "The House of the ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 24:1-25:19 is almost entirely rules for everyday life, such as divorce, loans, wages, gleaning, lashes, levirate marriage and weights. The walkthrough gives it full stops of story and choice cards. prep-walkthrough.md lists 'rules for everyday life' as a long stretch that gets one summary story card and no choice cards, with Exodus 21-23 as the example. It also says speeches and teaching are not long stretches. This passage is part of Moses' speech, so the two rules conflict.
findings.question: When a whole Sermons passage is a run of everyday laws inside a speech, like Deuteronomy 24-25, does it count as a long stretch with one summary card and no choice cards? Or does it get full story and choice cards because it is part of Moses' speech?

findings.problem: The question says 'her second marriage' and 'her first husband' without saying who she is. It relies on the story cards before it, which are no longer on screen. Name her, for example 'a divorced woman.'

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'flee' is not a penalty a law would set, so it is not believable. It is also not the same kind of thing as 'die' and 'repay.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The line 'follow every instruction from the ones he has given commands to about it' is hard to follow. It reads as a dodge to hide the answer, and the moment doesn't make sense. It also says Moses' commands to them were about skin disease, which the text doesn't specify. Set up the choice in plain words, for example 'follow the people God put in charge of it.'

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Story card 12 already says the lender doesn't go into the house. That rules out both wrong answers, 'Inside at his table' and 'In his storeroom with him,' which leaves only the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Under this law' points to nothing. The card before it is about wages, and no card has introduced the law about who is put to death for whose sin.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'That forgotten sheaf' points back to story card 8, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say it's harvest or that the farmer left a sheaf in the field.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'The same goes for' points back to earlier cards without saying what 'the same' is: leaving what remains for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'So his brother isn't degraded in their sight,' uses Bible wording ('brother,' 'degraded in their sight'). The two wrong answers are plain modern phrasing, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question says the ox walks over the grain 'all day.' Deuteronomy 25:4 gives no time, only 'while it is treading out the grain.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The joke makes 'a baker' the cheat with two differently sized scoops. The players are called bakers, so the joke laughs at them instead of at Papa Dorin. Make him the joke, or use someone who isn't a baker.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.

findings.problem: Story card 15 introduces the Amalekites as 'one more thing to remember.' That gives away the answer to card 17, which asks whether Israel can forget what Amalek did. Card 15 could tell what happened without framing it as something to remember.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
